world.title: US judge blocks Trump visa limits for students, journalists
world.summary: A federal judge in Boston on Monday temporarily blocked the Trump administration from enforcing new rules that would limit how long foreign students, exchange visitors and journalists could remain in the United States without applying for extensions. The preliminary injunction came one day before the Department of Home
world.content: A federal judge in Boston on Monday temporarily blocked the Trump administration from enforcing new rules that would limit how long foreign students, exchange visitors and journalists could remain in the United States without applying for extensions. The preliminary injunction came one day before the Department of Homeland Security rules were scheduled to take effect, leaving the existing system in place while litigation continues. The proposed policy would generally cap student and exchange-visitor stays at four years and limit foreign journalists to 240 days, with extensions available. Chinese journalists would face 90-day periods. District Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV said DHS relied on “exceptionally weak” rationales for restrictions based on national security and visa fraud, and failed to adequately consider public concerns or less burdensome alternatives. Saylor did not rule on the case's merits and scheduled another hearing for October 2.
world.image_alt: US judge blocks Trump visa limits for students, journalists

world.title: Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish leaders sign independence pact
world.summary: The leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland signed a memorandum of understanding in Cardiff on September 14 that calls on the UK government to “prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change” in each territory. Scottish First Minister John Swinney, Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland
world.content: The leaders of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland signed a memorandum of understanding in Cardiff on September 14 that calls on the UK government to “prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change” in each territory. Scottish First Minister John Swinney, Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth and Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O’Neill signed it alongside Sinn Féin president Mary Lou McDonald, acting as party leaders rather than representatives at a formal intergovernmental meeting. The parties said their nations have a right to determine their constitutional futures, that their future lies in the European Union, and that they would cooperate on the economy, energy and international affairs. The agreement followed President Trump’s weekend comments that he would “love to see” a united Ireland. The UK government has rejected immediate new independence votes, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s office saying it is focused on household finances and economic security rather than further constitutional referendums.
world.image_alt: Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish leaders sign independence pact

world.title: Pentagon watchdog reports munitions shortfall from Iran war
world.summary: A Pentagon inspector general report released Monday said the U.S. military’s Iran campaign led to strategic munitions shortages and exposed bottlenecks in the defense industry’s ability to replenish advanced weapons. Operation Epic Fury cost an estimated $33.4 billion between Feb. 28 and June 30, including $22.3 billio
world.content: A Pentagon inspector general report released Monday said the U.S. military’s Iran campaign led to strategic munitions shortages and exposed bottlenecks in the defense industry’s ability to replenish advanced weapons. Operation Epic Fury cost an estimated $33.4 billion between Feb. 28 and June 30, including $22.3 billion for expended munitions, $3.7 billion in equipment losses and $7.4 billion in other spending. The estimate excludes repairs to damaged facilities, aircraft replacement and replenishment of weapons stocks. The report also documented Iranian strikes that damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan. Listed losses included four F-15 aircraft destroyed, one F-35 damaged, seven KC-135 tankers damaged and up to 30 MQ-9 Reaper drones destroyed. The findings conflict with President Trump’s repeated claims that U.S. ammunition supplies were virtually unlimited. The report said the Pentagon is working to accelerate procurement and production.
world.image_alt: Pentagon watchdog reports munitions shortfall from Iran war

world.title: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia as Hormuz talks stall
world.summary: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed a new wave of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets on Monday, including King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait, while Saudi forces intensified airstrikes against Houthi positions along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. The attacks followed a rapid Houthi advance that offi
world.content: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed a new wave of missile and drone attacks on Saudi military targets on Monday, including King Khalid airbase in Khamis Mushait, while Saudi forces intensified airstrikes against Houthi positions along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. The attacks followed a rapid Houthi advance that officials said gave the group control of much of the western coast and strategic Perim Island at the entrance to the Red Sea. Gulf Arab states postponed a planned meeting in Oman with Iran on shipping arrangements through the Strait of Hormuz after Saudi Arabia sought a delay, according to Iran’s foreign ministry. Oman’s foreign minister said the postponement was made “in the interests of consensus,” while Iran said developments in Yemen were being used to divert attention from the causes of the crisis. Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline remains offline after an attack Riyadh blamed on Iran-backed Iraqi militias, and Brent crude reached about $108 a barrel on Monday.
world.image_alt: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia as Hormuz talks stall

world.title: Israel orders legal review of Gaza documentary
world.summary: Israel’s military chief, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, ordered the military prosecutor on Sept. 14 to examine possible legal action against the makers and participants in NAZA, an 80-minute documentary about Israel’s conduct in Gaza. Directed by Israeli journalists Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the film uses anonymous intervie
world.content: Israel’s military chief, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, ordered the military prosecutor on Sept. 14 to examine possible legal action against the makers and participants in NAZA, an 80-minute documentary about Israel’s conduct in Gaza. Directed by Israeli journalists Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the film uses anonymous interviews with 24 Israeli military and intelligence personnel who describe alleged targeting procedures, including AI-assisted systems and expected civilian casualties from strikes. The Israel Defense Forces rejected the film’s allegations, including a claim that an attack was approved with an expected toll of 500 civilian deaths, calling the assertion “completely false”. The order followed NAZA’s Special Jury Prize at the 83rd Venice Film Festival, where its premiere received about 25 minutes of standing applause. Culture Minister Miki Zohar asked authorities to investigate how the film obtained its material and whether its production or publication aided an enemy. He also called for the filmmakers’ citizenship to be revoked on treason grounds. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described the film as part of global antisemitic incitement and said it portrayed Israeli forces as war criminals.
world.image_alt: Israel orders legal review of Gaza documentary

world.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
world.summary: NATO fighter jets shot down an unidentified drone after it entered Lithuanian airspace shortly after midnight on Sept. 15, Lithuanian officials said. The aircraft was destroyed about 30 minutes later over a rural area near Pratkunai, close to Kaunas, after air-raid alerts were issued in Vilnius and surrounding areas. P
world.content: NATO fighter jets shot down an unidentified drone after it entered Lithuanian airspace shortly after midnight on Sept. 15, Lithuanian officials said. The aircraft was destroyed about 30 minutes later over a rural area near Pratkunai, close to Kaunas, after air-raid alerts were issued in Vilnius and surrounding areas. Preliminary information cited by Lithuanian national radio LRT indicated that the drone entered from neighboring Belarus and was traveling west, but officials said its origin, type and intended target remained under investigation. President Gitanas Nauseda thanked the alliance and said Lithuania would defend its airspace with NATO allies. The episode followed another reported drone alert in Lithuania on Sept. 13.
world.image_alt: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania

world.title: Trump EPA repeals power-plant emissions limits
world.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency repealed Biden-era limits on greenhouse-gas emissions from coal-fired and new natural gas power plants, reversing rules finalized in 2024 under the Clean Air Act. The rules would have required covered facilities to cut carbon dioxide emissions by up to 90% through carbon-capture tech
world.content: The Environmental Protection Agency repealed Biden-era limits on greenhouse-gas emissions from coal-fired and new natural gas power plants, reversing rules finalized in 2024 under the Clean Air Act. The rules would have required covered facilities to cut carbon dioxide emissions by up to 90% through carbon-capture technology or retire affected facilities; the EPA said the rules relied on technologies that were not adequately demonstrated and imposed unrealistic compliance demands. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the repeal at a G20 energy ministers’ meeting in Houston, saying the action would reduce regulatory costs, support new generating infrastructure and protect affordable energy. The agency also proposed barring future administrations from regulating greenhouse-gas emissions from power plants, a step expected to face legal challenges. The EPA estimates the rollback will eliminate more than $300 billion in industry costs, while environmental groups say it will increase health risks and pollution.
world.image_alt: Trump EPA repeals power-plant emissions limits

world.title: US Space Force confirms weapons deployed in orbit
world.summary: The United States has publicly confirmed for the first time that it has deployed “on-orbit space control weapons,” saying the systems can defend joint forces against hostile actions. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink disclosed the deployment on September 14 at the Air, Space & Cyber Conference in National Harbor, Maryland
world.content: The United States has publicly confirmed for the first time that it has deployed “on-orbit space control weapons,” saying the systems can defend joint forces against hostile actions. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink disclosed the deployment on September 14 at the Air, Space & Cyber Conference in National Harbor, Maryland. Officials did not identify the weapons, say how many are deployed, or state when they reached orbit. Meink said the disclosure was deliberate and important for deterrence, and that its wording had been carefully considered. US officials have cited Russian and Chinese efforts to develop systems that could attack or disrupt American satellites. The Trump administration has linked space capabilities and interceptor missiles to its planned Golden Dome missile-defense system.
world.image_alt: US Space Force confirms weapons deployed in orbit

business.title: Supreme Court blocks Trump mail ballot restrictions before midterms
business.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected President Donald Trump’s request to lift a lower-court order blocking new U.S. Postal Service requirements for mail-in ballots. The decision allows states to continue sending ballots under existing procedures as voting in the 2026 midterm elections had already begun. Trump’s Ma
business.content: The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday rejected President Donald Trump’s request to lift a lower-court order blocking new U.S. Postal Service requirements for mail-in ballots. The decision allows states to continue sending ballots under existing procedures as voting in the 2026 midterm elections had already begun. Trump’s March executive order directed the Postal Service to impose tighter controls, including requirements involving voter lists, standardized envelopes and barcodes. Justice Brett Kavanaugh agreed that the rules should not apply in 2026 because officials lacked enough time to implement them, while Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented.
business.image_alt: Supreme Court blocks Trump mail ballot restrictions before midterms

business.title: AI leaders urge slowdown as global stocks retreat
business.summary: Artificial-intelligence stocks fell across markets on Monday after Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei and OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman called for slower AI development to improve safety. Nvidia fell 2.7%, Intel nearly 6%, and other chipmakers also declined; the S&P 500 fell 0.48% and the Nasdaq Composite dropp
business.content: Artificial-intelligence stocks fell across markets on Monday after Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei and OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman called for slower AI development to improve safety. Nvidia fell 2.7%, Intel nearly 6%, and other chipmakers also declined; the S&P 500 fell 0.48% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.56%. Altman also said OpenAI would likely delay a Wall Street stock sale until next year, postponing a potential source of proceeds for early investors such as SoftBank. Oil prices and bond yields also weighed on markets as investors monitored renewed Middle East tensions and awaited U.S. and Japanese central-bank meetings. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5%, while Asian markets traded mixed on Tuesday; Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.8% in morning trading, Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.9%, and South Korea’s Kospi was little changed.

business.title: Trump EPA repeals power-plant emissions limits, cites $300 billion in savings
business.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency has repealed Biden-era carbon-emissions standards for coal-fired and new natural-gas power plants, eliminating requirements for covered facilities to sharply cut carbon pollution or install carbon-capture technology. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the action on September 14 a
business.content: The Environmental Protection Agency has repealed Biden-era carbon-emissions standards for coal-fired and new natural-gas power plants, eliminating requirements for covered facilities to sharply cut carbon pollution or install carbon-capture technology. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the action on September 14 at a G20 energy ministers meeting in Houston, describing it as an effort to reduce regulatory costs, support power generation and lower electricity prices. The 2024 standards would have required covered plants to control up to 90% of their carbon pollution, with utilities choosing between installing emissions-control technology and retiring coal plants in the 2030s. The EPA says the repeal will eliminate more than $300 billion in industry costs. The agency is also proposing to withdraw remaining greenhouse-gas requirements for power plants, arguing that the Clean Air Act does not authorize such regulation. Environmental groups say they will challenge the action in court, and the rule is expected to face immediate legal challenges.
business.image_alt: Trump EPA repeals power-plant emissions limits, cites $300 billion in savings

business.title: Fed expected to raise rates as Warsh faces Trump pressure
business.summary: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, Sept. 16, after holding rates steady and marking the first increase under Chair Kevin Warsh. Futures markets placed the probability of a hike above 90% on Sept. 14 and 15, while economists generally expected the
business.content: The Federal Reserve is widely expected to raise its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, Sept. 16, after holding rates steady and marking the first increase under Chair Kevin Warsh. Futures markets placed the probability of a hike above 90% on Sept. 14 and 15, while economists generally expected the target range to rise from 3.5%-3.75% to 3.75%-4%. The meeting began Sept. 15 and is scheduled to conclude Sept. 16. The expected move follows August inflation data showing consumer prices up 3.4% from a year earlier and core CPI up 0.3% from July, or 2.4% annually, while oil prices rose above $100 a barrel as fighting involving Iran intensified. Warsh said at the Federal Reserve’s Jackson Hole conference two weeks earlier that inflation had not yet been brought under control. President Trump has repeatedly called for lower rates and recently threatened to halt trade with some countries if the Fed did not ease policy.
business.image_alt: Fed expected to raise rates as Warsh faces Trump pressure

business.title: China’s August data show weaker demand, stronger factory output
business.summary: China’s domestic economy weakened further in August as retail sales rose 0.4% from a year earlier, below July’s 0.6% increase and economists’ 0.8% forecast. Fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% in the first eight months from a year earlier, the steepest decline since April 2020, while the urban surveyed unemployment rate r
business.content: China’s domestic economy weakened further in August as retail sales rose 0.4% from a year earlier, below July’s 0.6% increase and economists’ 0.8% forecast. Fixed-asset investment fell 7.2% in the first eight months from a year earlier, the steepest decline since April 2020, while the urban surveyed unemployment rate rose to 5.3% from 5.2% in July. Industrial output rose 5.2% year on year after 4.5% growth in July, exceeding the 4.8% market forecast. The National Bureau of Statistics said supply remained strong while demand was weak, and called for stronger macroeconomic adjustment, higher domestic demand and industrial upgrading. Second-quarter growth slowed to 4.3%, below Beijing’s 4.5%-5% annual target range.
business.image_alt: China’s August data show weaker demand, stronger factory output

business.title: Update: Trump accepts ethics rules ahead of crypto bill vote
business.summary: President Trump has accepted revised ethics restrictions in the Senate’s 635-page CLARITY Act, removing an obstacle in Republican-Democratic negotiations before a procedural vote scheduled for Tuesday, Sept. 15. The bill would divide federal oversight of digital assets between the Securities and Exchange Commission and
business.content: President Trump has accepted revised ethics restrictions in the Senate’s 635-page CLARITY Act, removing an obstacle in Republican-Democratic negotiations before a procedural vote scheduled for Tuesday, Sept. 15. The bill would divide federal oversight of digital assets between the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The latest text would require covered federal officials and their spouses to divest significant crypto holdings or place them in a blind trust, and would bar them from issuing or sponsoring digital assets. The agreement does not guarantee passage. Republicans hold 53 Senate seats and need at least seven Democratic votes to reach the 60-vote cloture threshold. Democrats sent Republicans a counterproposal after reviewing the latest text, while state attorneys general and banking groups continued to oppose parts of the bill. The House passed its version 294-134 in July 2025, and the Senate Banking Committee advanced its version 15-9 in May 2026.
business.image_alt: Update: Trump accepts ethics rules ahead of crypto bill vote

business.title: Dangote launches $1.6 billion refinery IPO in Nigeria
business.summary: Aliko Dangote opened a public offering for 4.1 billion shares in his Lagos-based petroleum refinery on September 14, seeking 2.15 trillion naira, or about $1.6 billion, in what would be Africa’s largest initial public offering. The shares are priced at 525 naira each, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares, and the o
business.content: Aliko Dangote opened a public offering for 4.1 billion shares in his Lagos-based petroleum refinery on September 14, seeking 2.15 trillion naira, or about $1.6 billion, in what would be Africa’s largest initial public offering. The shares are priced at 525 naira each, with a minimum subscription of 10 shares, and the offer remains open until October 13. Dangote will retain an 87% stake. Sources value the refinery at roughly $47 billion to $49 billion. The proceeds will help fund a planned $14.3 billion expansion that would increase processing capacity from 700,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million by 2028, while adding petrochemical and refining units. Dangote has marketed the IPO to retail investors across Africa, but analysts and prospective buyers have questioned whether the valuation fully reflects the expansion plans. A private placement in July raised $2.5 billion for a 6% stake at a lower implied valuation.
business.image_alt: Dangote launches $1.6 billion refinery IPO in Nigeria

business.title: Carney courts global capital and deeper EU ties for Canada
business.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney opened the first Canada Investment Summit in Toronto on Sept. 14, seeking to attract capital for more than 160 projects and reduce the country’s reliance on the United States during an escalating trade dispute. About 300 chief executives and senior investment officials are attending,
business.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney opened the first Canada Investment Summit in Toronto on Sept. 14, seeking to attract capital for more than 160 projects and reduce the country’s reliance on the United States during an escalating trade dispute. About 300 chief executives and senior investment officials are attending, representing firms and funds that collectively manage more than C$120 trillion. Ottawa is targeting C$1 trillion in investment over the next five years. The government’s pitch highlights energy, critical minerals, infrastructure, technology and defence, including 11 oil and gas megaprojects and 31 clean-energy developments. Carney is also travelling to Europe to seek a tailored strategic partnership with the European Union, rather than EU membership or arrangements modelled on Norway or Switzerland. Ottawa says discussions could cover investment, trade, labour mobility, energy, artificial intelligence, defence and critical minerals. A senior Canadian official said the proposed arrangement could allow Canadians to live and work in Europe without visas. Canada sends roughly 70% of its exports to the United States. Carney is scheduled to attend European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union address on Sept. 16 and address the European Parliament on Sept. 17.
business.image_alt: Carney courts global capital and deeper EU ties for Canada

science.title: Brain implant decodes speech and gestures for paralyzed patients
science.summary: Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, developed a brain-computer interface that simultaneously decodes attempted speech and upper-body movements, allowing people with severe paralysis to control personalized full-body digital avatars. The study, published in Nature Neuroscience on Sept. 14, involv
science.content: Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco, developed a brain-computer interface that simultaneously decodes attempted speech and upper-body movements, allowing people with severe paralysis to control personalized full-body digital avatars. The study, published in Nature Neuroscience on Sept. 14, involved three participants with severe paralysis and translated brain activity into avatar commands rather than speech alone. One participant achieved 100% accuracy for both speech and gesture in three assessments, while two participants controlled personalized avatars using the combined system.
science.image_alt: Brain implant decodes speech and gestures for paralyzed patients

science.title: Singapore ash landfill becomes habitat for coral and mangroves
science.summary: Singapore has operated Semakau Landfill, an offshore waste facility about eight kilometers from the main island, since 1999. The 350-hectare site is enclosed by a seven-kilometer rock bund and receives ash produced after Singapore burns nearly all its garbage. The site has replanted mangroves and living coral and hosts
science.content: Singapore has operated Semakau Landfill, an offshore waste facility about eight kilometers from the main island, since 1999. The 350-hectare site is enclosed by a seven-kilometer rock bund and receives ash produced after Singapore burns nearly all its garbage. The site has replanted mangroves and living coral and hosts guided nature walks for visitors to spot migratory birds. Separately, reef structures installed off Small Sister’s Island in 2018 had accumulated 95 coral colonies from seven genera by February 2022, including colonies on two structures that had not been planted.
science.image_alt: Singapore ash landfill becomes habitat for coral and mangroves

science.title: Researchers trace Britain’s Devil’s Arrows stones to a site 11 miles away
science.summary: Researchers have identified Brimham Rocks in North Yorkshire as the geological source of the stones used to build the Devil’s Arrows, a prehistoric standing-stone row near Boroughbridge in northern England. The stones came from at least 18 kilometers (11 miles) away, weigh more than 25 tonnes, and reach up to 7 meters
science.content: Researchers have identified Brimham Rocks in North Yorkshire as the geological source of the stones used to build the Devil’s Arrows, a prehistoric standing-stone row near Boroughbridge in northern England. The stones came from at least 18 kilometers (11 miles) away, weigh more than 25 tonnes, and reach up to 7 meters (23 feet) high. The finding indicates that the builders selected a distant, difficult source rather than using the nearest available rock, though the reason remains unclear. Related archaeological reports describe Neanderthals arranging more than two tonnes of broken stone into rings 336 meters inside a French cave about 176,000 years ago, and a central French site preserving evidence of human occupation from the Paleolithic through the Middle Ages.
science.image_alt: Researchers trace Britain’s Devil’s Arrows stones to a site 11 miles away

science.title: NASA selects 12 studies on space crops and astronaut health
science.summary: NASA selected 12 new investigations to support human exploration beyond Earth: six on producing food in space and six on how spaceflight conditions affect astronaut health and physiology. The studies support NASA's lunar and Mars exploration goals and will examine edible plants, plant-associated microbial communities,
science.content: NASA selected 12 new investigations to support human exploration beyond Earth: six on producing food in space and six on how spaceflight conditions affect astronaut health and physiology. The studies support NASA's lunar and Mars exploration goals and will examine edible plants, plant-associated microbial communities, extreme-dryness survival mechanisms, and algae biology relevant to spaceflight. NASA announced the selections on September 14, 2026.
science.image_alt: NASA selects 12 studies on space crops and astronaut health

science.title: CERN researchers study cosmic-ray showers with oxygen–proton collisions
science.summary: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider conducted the first laboratory collisions of oxygen atoms and protons to simulate cosmic rays. Cosmic rays strike atoms in Earth’s atmosphere, producing particle showers that reach the ground; scientists have studied these showers for more than a century but do not yet fully u
science.content: Physicists at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider conducted the first laboratory collisions of oxygen atoms and protons to simulate cosmic rays. Cosmic rays strike atoms in Earth’s atmosphere, producing particle showers that reach the ground; scientists have studied these showers for more than a century but do not yet fully understand how they form. The experiment allows researchers to examine the formation of these particle showers under controlled conditions rather than relying solely on observations from the sky.
science.image_alt: CERN researchers study cosmic-ray showers with oxygen–proton collisions

science.title: Scientists say water limits could constrain sustainable lunar cities
science.summary: Researchers Martin Elvis of the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and Jonathan McDowell say a self-sustaining city on the Moon would face a finite water supply despite confirmed ice deposits in permanently shadowed polar craters. Their analysis, published in *Frontiers in Space Technologies*, finds that a populatio
science.content: Researchers Martin Elvis of the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and Jonathan McDowell say a self-sustaining city on the Moon would face a finite water supply despite confirmed ice deposits in permanently shadowed polar craters. Their analysis, published in *Frontiers in Space Technologies*, finds that a population of 1 million would exhaust an optimistic estimate of roughly 1 billion tonnes of lunar water after about a century with water recycling at around 98%, comparable to the International Space Station. The researchers say a settlement of up to 10,000 people would be more plausible. Lower estimates of lunar water reserves could leave even a relatively small city short of water after about a decade. Energy appears less restrictive: polar sites with near-continuous sunlight could support large solar installations, but the analysis identifies water for drinking, oxygen, hydrogen and rocket propellant as the limiting resource.
science.image_alt: Scientists say water limits could constrain sustainable lunar cities

science.title: Summer 2026 brings record heat and wildfires across several regions
science.summary: Summer 2026 brought extreme conditions across several regions, including prolonged rain followed by drought, repeated heatwaves and wildfires in Britain, record heat in the United States, and an exceptionally hot summer in France. In England’s West Midlands, dry vegetation helped fires spread, while a major blaze in St
science.content: Summer 2026 brought extreme conditions across several regions, including prolonged rain followed by drought, repeated heatwaves and wildfires in Britain, record heat in the United States, and an exceptionally hot summer in France. In England’s West Midlands, dry vegetation helped fires spread, while a major blaze in Stourbridge destroyed 19 homes. Fires scorched areas including Cannock Chase and Sheldon Country Park, killing wildlife and altering soil and ash chemistry. The Guardian cited an estimate that the 2003 European heatwave killed about 70,000 people and said extreme heat caused more Australian deaths than bushfires, floods, storms and cyclones combined between 2000 and 2018.
science.image_alt: Summer 2026 brings record heat and wildfires across several regions

science.title: UN report says exceeding 1.5°C warming limit is now unavoidable
science.summary: A new United Nations climate assessment says the world is set to exceed the 1.5-degree-Celsius warming threshold associated with the 2015 Paris Agreement, ending the possibility of keeping warming below that level without a period of exceedance. The assessment has forced vulnerable countries that advocated for the targ
science.content: A new United Nations climate assessment says the world is set to exceed the 1.5-degree-Celsius warming threshold associated with the 2015 Paris Agreement, ending the possibility of keeping warming below that level without a period of exceedance. The assessment has forced vulnerable countries that advocated for the target to confront the prospect of exceeding a threshold they considered central to protection against climate damage. Global warming is expected to pass 1.5°C within the next five years, while current policies point to about 2.6°C of warming by 2100, according to the supplied reporting. Projected consequences include faster ice-sheet loss and severe damage to coral reefs.
science.image_alt: UN report says exceeding 1.5°C warming limit is now unavoidable

sports.title: Maresca leads Manchester City past United with ten men
sports.summary: Enzo Maresca has won each of his first five Premier League and Champions League matches as Manchester City manager since succeeding Pep Guardiola. City beat Manchester United 1-0 at Old Trafford on Sunday despite playing most of the match with 10 players after Phil Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute. The result left
sports.content: Enzo Maresca has won each of his first five Premier League and Champions League matches as Manchester City manager since succeeding Pep Guardiola. City beat Manchester United 1-0 at Old Trafford on Sunday despite playing most of the match with 10 players after Phil Foden was sent off in the 23rd minute. The result left City joint-top of the Premier League with Arsenal after four league victories. After Foden's dismissal, Maresca delayed major changes, moved Rayan Cherki to the right and replaced him with Iliman Ndiaye at half-time as City protected their lead and denied United space behind the defence.
sports.image_alt: Maresca leads Manchester City past United with ten men

sports.title: Drew Brees considered Broncos comeback after Bo Nix injury
sports.summary: Former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees seriously considered coming out of retirement to play for the Denver Broncos in last season’s AFC Championship Game, ESPN reported. Denver explored the possibility after starter Bo Nix suffered a season-ending ankle injury in the divisional-round victory over Buffalo. Fo
sports.content: Former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees seriously considered coming out of retirement to play for the Denver Broncos in last season’s AFC Championship Game, ESPN reported. Denver explored the possibility after starter Bo Nix suffered a season-ending ankle injury in the divisional-round victory over Buffalo. Former Broncos offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and assistant Pete Carmichael, who had coached Brees in New Orleans, contacted him. Brees, who turned 47 two days before Nix’s injury, wanted to work out before deciding. He later experienced wrist discomfort and declined a comeback, leaving Jarrett Stidham to start against New England. Stidham completed 17 of 31 passes for 133 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Denver’s 10-7 AFC Championship loss.
sports.image_alt: Drew Brees considered Broncos comeback after Bo Nix injury

sports.title: Tottenham exclude Richarlison for Liverpool Carabao Cup clash
sports.summary: Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi ruled Richarlison out of Tuesday’s Carabao Cup third-round match against Liverpool at Anfield. The Brazil forward remains eligible for the competition despite his omission from Spurs’ 25-man Premier League squad. Tottenham have yet to score a Premier League goal after four mat
sports.content: Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi ruled Richarlison out of Tuesday’s Carabao Cup third-round match against Liverpool at Anfield. The Brazil forward remains eligible for the competition despite his omission from Spurs’ 25-man Premier League squad. Tottenham have yet to score a Premier League goal after four matches. Richarlison’s proposed summer moves to Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama broke down. TeamTalk reports that Shabab Al-Ahli remain interested, with the UAE Pro League transfer window open until September 28. Liverpool are unbeaten but drew 0-0 with Fulham, while Tottenham’s only win in all competitions was a 5-1 Carabao Cup victory over Charlton on August 26.
sports.image_alt: Tottenham exclude Richarlison for Liverpool Carabao Cup clash

sports.title: Arsenal weigh January loan for winger Noni Madueke
sports.summary: Arsenal may need to decide Noni Madueke’s future before the January transfer window, with Atlético Madrid and Juventus reportedly monitoring the 24-year-old England winger. A loan, potentially with an option to buy, is the likeliest structure. Madueke joined Arsenal from Chelsea in 2025 for a reported fee of about £52
sports.content: Arsenal may need to decide Noni Madueke’s future before the January transfer window, with Atlético Madrid and Juventus reportedly monitoring the 24-year-old England winger. A loan, potentially with an option to buy, is the likeliest structure. Madueke joined Arsenal from Chelsea in 2025 for a reported fee of about £52 million and gained opportunities during Bukayo Saka’s absences in his first season. Saka’s return to full fitness has limited Madueke’s opportunities: he has made only substitute appearances in the Premier League this season, and Arsenal are considering whether a temporary move would give him more regular playing time.

sports.content: England back-rower Henry Pollock has yet to re-sign with Northampton Saints and is considering offers from overseas clubs and opportunities in other sports as negotiations over a contract extension continue. The 21-year-old’s current agreement expires after the forthcoming campaign, and Northampton is widely expected to remain his preferred destination after he joined the club’s academy and helped it win the Premiership title in June. Pollock’s agent, Eddie Hearn, has described him as a potential seven-figure player, while reports say Northampton has offered a substantial pay rise. Pollock said rugby remains his immediate priority but that his career is short, making it important to consider options that could include playing abroad or eventually trying boxing, MMA or another sport.

sports.content: Arsenal will contact refereeing body Pro Ref for an explanation of the penalty awarded to Sunderland in Saturday’s 2-0 Premier League defeat at the Stadium of Light. Referee John Brooks penalised Ezri Konsa after a tussle with Dan Ballard at a corner, and VAR confirmed the decision; Arsenal want clarity on both judgments. David Raya saved Enzo Le Fée’s spot-kick before Bruno Guimaraes and Bukayo Saka scored in Arsenal’s win. Mikel Arteta criticised the decision after the match, saying it could have changed the result and affected the title race, while the Premier League Match Centre said VAR had checked and confirmed the penalty call.

sports.title: Kawhi Leonard returns to Raptors after delayed trade

Toronto sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, a 2027 first-round swap and t
sports.content: The Toronto Raptors and Los Angeles Clippers completed their long-delayed trade for Kawhi Leonard on Monday, Sept. 14, sending the seven-time All-Star back to the team he led to its first NBA championship in 2019. Toronto sent Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, a 2027 first-round swap and two second-round picks to Los Angeles. The teams initially agreed to the deal on June 30, but Toronto paused the transaction while the NBA investigated possible salary-cap circumvention involving Leonard and the Clippers. The league concluded its probe on Sept. 2 and fined Leonard $700,000 and the Clippers $30 million, stripped the Clippers of five first-round picks from 2029 through 2033, and suspended senior executives. The original trade terms remained unchanged after the findings.

sports.content: Formula 1 organizers in Madrid have told F1 and the FIA they are ready to modify Madring before the 2027 Spanish Grand Prix, after the circuit’s inaugural race produced very few overtaking opportunities. Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli won ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen and McLaren’s Lando Norris, but drivers said the layout made it difficult to follow closely or attempt passes. The circuit earned praise for its challenge over one qualifying lap and its facilities, but the race was criticized as processional. Organizers have received FIA recommendations, and track managing director Luis Garcia Abad said the venue has enough space for changes. Proposed ideas include revising the Turn 5/6 area and creating stronger overtaking opportunities elsewhere on the lap. Norris also lost the lead after a Virtual Safety Car was called just after he passed the pit entry, prompting debate over the rules as well as criticism of the circuit.
